title: Finite L¹ nets on countably many sets give one subsequence converging in L¹ on each of them (steps 0 and 2–4 of the diagonal extraction)
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let Q_j ⊆ ℝⁿ (j ∈ ℕ) be arbitrary sets and u_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) functions such that every u_k is Lebesgue integrable on every Q_j, and such that for every j and every ε > 0 there is a finite set F ⊆ ℕ with: every k ∈ ℕ has some i ∈ F with ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖u_k(x) − u_i(x)‖ₑ dx < ofReal ε. Then there are a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ and functions G_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ (j ∈ ℕ) such that every G_j is integrable on Q_j and, for every j, ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖u_{ψ(k)}(x) − G_j(x)‖ₑ dx → 0 as k → ∞.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (Q : ℕ → Set (Rn n)) (u : ℕ → Rn n → ℝ), (∀ j k, IntegrableOn (u k) (Q j) volume) → (∀ j, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ F : Finset ℕ, ∀ k, ∃ i ∈ F, (∫⁻ x in Q j, ‖u k x - u i x‖ₑ) < ENNReal.ofReal ε) → ∃ (ψ : ℕ → ℕ) (G : ℕ → Rn n → ℝ), StrictMono ψ ∧ (∀ j, IntegrableOn (G j) (Q j) volume) ∧ ∀ j, Tendsto (fun k ↦ ∫⁻ x in Q j, ‖u (ψ k) x - G j x‖ₑ) atTop (𝓝 0)
